extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instructions: 10,000 language-language conflicts and 10,000 vision-language conflicts. It covers eight tasks: RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict. SCI-All contains the complete dataset; SCI-Base and SCI-Core are manually selected subsets containing 10% and 1% of SCI-All, respectively.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.citeAs: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang. Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2, 5 August 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SCI was constructed using AutoCreate, an automatic dataset creation framework combining programs and large language models. A small batch of manually supplied task-relevant seeds initializes a seed pool. Language and visual loops each apply a generator, decorator, and cleaner: generators create initial text or images, decorators introduce self-contradictions, and cleaners remove data that fails quality standards. Human experts and LLMs double-check generated data, and new seeds extracted from accepted data are returned to the seed pool for further iterations. Human experts rigorously checked the final dataset. SemanticConflict additionally uses images retrieved from the ImageNet-1k validation set.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include manually supplied task-relevant seeds, handcrafted mutually exclusive instruction pairs, LLM-generated texts, rules, fictitious object descriptions, entities, questions, and numerical data, and programmatically generated text images, charts, and geometric images. SemanticConflict is the only task using external data: ImageNet-1k validation images and class names.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Contradictions are deliberately introduced by pairing rules with violating sentences, appending opposite attribute descriptions to fictitious object descriptions, combining mutually exclusive instructions, and pairing forbidden-word restrictions with questions requiring those words. OCRConflict renders one instruction and a sentence as an image and supplies a conflicting textual instruction. FigureConflict changes the largest numerical value to the smallest before plotting the chart. GeometricConflict alters object descriptions to refer to nonexistent combinations of attributes. SemanticConflict replaces correct ImageNet class names in questions with randomly selected similar but different objects. Fonts, sizes, colors, and chart styles are varied during image generation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: AutoCreate's cleaner excludes generated data that does not meet quality standards. Both LLMs and human experts double-check generated data, and human experts rigorously check the final dataset. For ForbbidenConflict, an LLM agent checks whether generated questions have unique answers, addressing the tendency of LLMs to generate ambiguous questions. SCI-Base and SCI-Core are manually selected from SCI-All; ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict require additional effort to guarantee diversity in SCI-Core.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is organized into eight conflict types defined by their construction procedures. Conflicting instructions are generated automatically using programs and LLMs, and human experts check dataset quality. SemanticConflict uses ImageNet class names to retrieve images and generate questions, then substitutes those names with similar but different objects to create conflicts. The paper does not describe a separate human item-labeling protocol.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For evaluation of model responses, human experts and GPT-4 independently assessed replies generated on SCI-Core to determine whether they identified the input conflict. Agreement was measured using Spearman correlation and concordance: GPT-4V replies had a correlation of 0.881 and 94% concordance, LLaVA-1.5 replies had 0.999 and 99%, and Gemini replies had 0.854 and 97%. These analyses concern response evaluation rather than aggregation of dataset item annotations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: AutoCreate uses LLMs and programs for automatic conflict construction and quality checking; an LLM agent checks answer uniqueness for ForbbidenConflict. GPT-4, ChatGPT, and ChatGLM are used as evaluation agents to judge whether model responses recognize conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that more modalities will be included in SCI using AutoCreate. No update schedule, maintainer assignment, dataset versioning policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: SCI provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance multimodal models' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The authors state that AutoCreate supports diverse instruction datasets and promotes inclusivity in AI research, while improved dissonance detection can foster trust and reliability in AI systems. The paper also motivates conflict detection through challenges faced by children, language beginners, and vulnerable populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SCI includes only language-language and vision-language paradigms. It provides no fine-grained control over the degree of conflict. The work does not include a detailed study of multimodal models' attention mechanisms when confronted with conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking large language and multimodal models on their ability to detect self-contradictory instructions. The paper evaluates zero-shot, chain-of-thought, few-shot, self-consistency, and Cognitive Awakening Prompting approaches. SCI-All, SCI-Base, and SCI-Core provide different dataset scales to cater to different evaluation needs. Performance is measured by the hit ratio: the proportion of model replies that successfully identify the conflict.
